The authors chose these substrate strains because they sufficiently exceed the saturation crack density: We chose substrate strains of 5%[2] and 10%[3]. Their tests covered a wider range overall, from strains of 0−10%[4], and the coatings were deformed up to subjected to axial tensile deformation up to 5%[5] and 10% strains[6] at a rate of 2 mm/min[7]. In short, the locked-in states correspond to 5%[8] and 10%[9] applied axial tensile strain on the NiTi substrate.
